paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Next slide. These are called pleasure beings — the top of the desire realm. They have really great bodies; they're kind of like demigods. But they also suffer from extreme forms of jealousy. They're kind of at war with each other. If you study classical Greek or Roman mythology, you'll read about all the gods at war with each other — they're really jealous of each other, and they interfere in the human realm a little bit. There are different words for these things; we're not going to go into the details. So there are different types of pleasure beings, still in the desire realm. Things are not bad enough there to motivate them to get out of suffering.

chapters.title: Bardo Beings — Between Death and Birth

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: All right, we'll finish with the next slide. There's another type of being called a Bardo being — a being in the bardo, in between death and birth. This is a painting by Alex Gray. It's called the Bardo Being. I wrote the title in Tibetan in my notes. The idea is that a Bardo being isn't really considered a type of birth — it's what happens in between. There's a long discussion of what those beings look like, and when they start to look like their next birth, and things like that. The Abhidharma talks about how long they stay there, in between death and birth. But just know that they're not technically considered one of the births — because a Bardo being can be in between any of the different realms.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So we're going to pause there. The way to think about this: we're cataloging all the different types of beings, how to become them, and how to motivate ourselves to avoid certain ones — so that we don't have to deal with that ever again.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: We'll continue the discussion after the break. We'll be back at seven o'clock — so, an hour and a half. In the next class, we're going to talk specifically about the yi-dak [YI DAGS], the craving spirits — what they're all about — and about animals as well, how beings get reborn there, and the specific kinds of suffering you have there. All right, take a break. Thank you, everyone online. We'll see you soon.
